newsitem.title: UK: Cathay urges airlines to publish cargo standards.
newsitem.headline: Cathay urges airlines to publish cargo standards.

text.p: Standard league tables listing airlines' cargo service performance standards should be published openly, said Cathay Pacific Airways' UK/Ireland cargo manager Mark Olney.
"At present, we have a number of airlines publishing their performance figures, but all based on a different set of rules," he said.
"We, the airlines, are generally committed to providing a quality performance level. As long as the standards are the same, I think most of us will publish the findings," he said.

Earlier, the UK Air Freight Forum had drafted standard measures of airline cargo performance based on all aspects of airfreight movement -- from shippers' premises to forwarders to airport delivery, waiting time before truck unloading and final delivery by airline to destination
The Forum comprises 20 leading airlines, forwarders and shippers operating in the UK market.

"The Forum hopes that once these standards have been consulted upon and finalised and introduced in the UK, hopefully by end-1997, they will be adopted by shippers, forwarders and airlines worldwide," said a statement issued by the Forum.

Andrew Traill, shipping and air manager of Forum member the British Shippers' Council (BSC), said that once the UK performance standard measures had been approved, they would be presented for consideration and anticipated adoption by the European Air Cargo Forum (EASC) in Brussels.
The EASC was formed in March to back the needs of the European airfreight industry.
-Bob Murphy, Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017
